mainTopic: The count of non-kosher birds, bird traditions (מסורת), and buying eggs from גויים
overview: The amud opens by supporting רב's count of 24 non-kosher birds. Since דברים comes to add to ויקרא, a bird name that shows up in only one list must be another name for a bird in the other list. That proves ראה = דאה, and אביי shows that איה = דיה. A ברייתא of רבי explains why the Torah still wrote both איה and דיה. רבי אבהו disagrees: he says the ראה is the איה, which joins all four names into one bird and leaves only 23. The גמרא then teaches that kosher birds are countless, so the Torah lists the non-kosher birds but the kosher animals, and it learns from this to teach students concisely. Next comes the rule that a kosher bird may be eaten based on a מסורת from a hunter who knows the birds and their names. The amud ends with buying eggs from גויים, and it asks why we don't just check the eggs' signs; that answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof that ראה and דאה are the same bird
steps.stepSummary: Each list has only one of the two names. This shows that ראה and דאה are one species.
steps.simpleTranslation: We assume דברים comes to add to the list in ויקרא. So why does ויקרא write 'דאה', while דברים writes 'ראה' and leaves out 'דאה'? We learn from this that ראה and דאה are one species.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that ראה and דאה are two names for one bird. This keeps the total number of non-kosher birds from growing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If דברים were only adding birds, it should have repeated דאה and added ראה. Instead, ראה stands where דאה stood. So ראה is not a new bird. It is the same bird under another name.

keyTerms.meaning: The book of דברים, which repeats much of the Torah
A non-kosher bird named in דברים
A non-kosher bird named in ויקרא

steps.title: The count still comes to twenty-five
steps.stepSummary: Even after joining ראה and דאה, the count is 25, not 24.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are still twenty-five birds!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the count of 24. Even after treating ראה and דאה as one bird, there is still one bird too many.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding the birds of both lists, minus the ראה/דאה overlap, still gives 25. So another pair of names must be one bird, or else רב's number is wrong.

phrases.english: But still, there are twenty-five?

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even with ראה and דאה counted as one bird, the total is still 25

steps.title: אביי: איה and דיה are also one bird
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that איה and דיה are one species, just like ראה and דאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Just as ראה and דאה are one, so too איה and דיה are one.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the problem of 25. He says a second pair of names, איה and דיה, also refers to one bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If איה and דיה are one bird, the total drops from 25 to 24. This matches רב's count. His proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-kosher bird named in both lists
A non-kosher bird named only in דברים

phrases.english: Abaye said:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁרָאָה וְדָאָה אַחַת הִיא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a second pair of names for one bird
steps.terutzHavaAmina: איה and דיה are two separate birds, making 25
steps.terutzMaskana: איה and דיה are one bird, so the total is 24

steps.title: Proof from where 'after its kind' is written
steps.stepSummary: ויקרא puts 'למינה' on the איה, and דברים puts it on the דיה. This shows they are one bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think they are two birds, ask this: דברים comes to add. So why does ויקרא put 'after its kind' on the איה, while דברים puts 'after its kind' on the דיה? We learn from this that איה and דיה are one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up אביי with the same kind of reasoning used for ראה and דאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'למינה' moved from the איה in ויקרא to the דיה in דברים. That shows the דיה is not a new bird. It describes the same bird as the איה.

keyTerms.meaning: If it would enter your mind; if you thought

steps.title: Why write both names?
steps.stepSummary: If איה and דיה are one bird, why does דברים list both?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that איה and דיה are one, why did the Torah need to write both איה and דיה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the Torah would use two names for one bird in the same verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating ראה in place of דאה makes sense, because the two names are in different books. But דברים names both איה and דיה side by side. That looks unnecessary if they are the same bird.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מֵאַחַר שֶׁאַיָּה וְדַיָּה אַחַת הִיא,
phrases.english: And now that ayya and dayya are one,
why does it need to write ayya and dayya?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר שֶׁאַיָּה וְדַיָּה אַחַת הִיא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the Torah wrote both names in דברים if they mean one bird

steps.title: רבי: so no one can claim a loophole
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי says both names were written so no one could argue that a bird called by the other name is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי says, I could have read only 'איה'. Why was 'דיה' stated? So as not to give someone room to argue. It should not happen that you call it איה and he calls it דיה, or you call it דיה and he calls it איה. That is why דברים writes: 'And the ראה, and the איה, and the דיה after its kind.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The Torah wrote both names so that the bird is forbidden whichever name people use for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People in different places called this bird by different names. If only one name were written, someone using the other name could claim his bird is not the forbidden one. Writing both closes that loophole, and the count stays at 24.

keyTerms.meaning: I could read; it would be enough to say
An opening for argument; an excuse

steps.whatToRemember: ראה/דאה are one bird, and איה/דיה are one bird. So both lists come to 24 non-kosher birds, as רב said.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rebbi says:
I could read 'ayya',
why was 'dayya' stated?
So as not to give an opening
to an opponent to disagree,
that it should not be that you call it ayya
and he calls it dayya,
phrases.notes: He means the other person would then say his 'dayya' isn't forbidden, and eat it.

phrases.aramaic: אַתָּה קוֹרֵא דַּיָּה וְהוּא קוֹרֵא אַיָּה,
phrases.english: or you call it dayya and he calls it ayya,
therefore it wrote in Deuteronomy:
'And the ra'a, and the ayya, and the dayya after its kind.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: אֶקְרָא אֲנִי אַיָּה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both names are written so no one can permit the bird by calling it by the other name

steps.title: A ברייתא implies the bird list adds a bird
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the bird list is repeated because of the ראה. This seems to mean the ראה is a new, added bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: Why were the lists repeated? For animals, because of the שסועה. For birds, because of the ראה. Isn't it clear that since the animal list there is repeated to add, the bird list is also repeated to add?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim that ראה is just another name for דאה, using a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שסועה is a truly new animal added in דברים. The ברייתא puts the ראה in the same position, so it seems the ראה is also a new bird. That would bring back the problem of too many birds.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a split hoof, listed only in דברים
Is it not that...? (introduces a suggested inference)

phrases.english: They raised an objection: Why were they repeated?
For animals, because of the shesua,
and for birds, because of the ra'a.
Is it not that since for animals there it is to add,
for birds too it is to add?

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ראה and דאה are one bird
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא pairs ראה with שסועה, which is an added animal, so ראה should be an added bird

steps.title: Animals: to add; birds: to explain
steps.stepSummary: The animal list repeats to add the שסועה. The bird list repeats only to explain that ראה is the same as דאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. There, by animals, it is to add. Here, by birds, it is to explain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the comparison. The two repeats have different purposes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only says each list was repeated because of one name. It does not say both names are new species. For birds, the name ראה is given to explain what the דאה is, so the count of 24 stands.
steps.whatToRemember: The animal list in דברים adds something new (the שסועה). The bird list only explains (ראה = דאה).

phrases.english: No, there it is to add,
here it is to explain.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the purpose of each repetition
steps.terutzMaskana: Animals: adds the שסועה. Birds: explains that ראה is דאה

steps.title: רבי אבהו says the ראה is the איה
steps.stepSummary: The view from the earlier steps disagrees with רבי אבהו, who says ראה is the same bird as איה. It is called ראה because it sees very well.
steps.simpleTranslation: This argues with רבי אבהו. He said: the ראה is the איה. Why is it called ראה? Because it sees extremely well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings in רבי אבהו, who has a different way of matching up the bird names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, ראה was paired with דאה, and איה was paired with דיה. רבי אבהו instead says ראה is the איה. He explains the name ראה from the word רואה, meaning 'sees'.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-kosher bird named in דברים
A non-kosher bird named in both lists

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Abbahu
for Rabbi Abbahu says:
The ra'a is the ayya.
And why is it called ra'a?
Because it sees extremely well.
phrases.notes: The name ראה sounds like רואה, which means 'sees'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a view that differs from steps 1-8, which made two separate pairs (ראה = דאה, איה = דיה). רבי אבהו links ראה to איה, which joins the pairs into one bird (worked out in steps 11-14).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ראה is the same bird as איה, named for its sharp eyesight.

steps.title: Proof that the איה has sharp eyes
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in איוב connects the איה with seeing, and a ברייתא says it can stand in בבל and see a carcass in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'That path no bird of prey knows, and the eye of the איה has not seen it.' A ברייתא teaches: it stands in בבל and sees a carcass in ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רבי אבהו's point that the איה is the bird known for its powerful eyesight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of 'the eye of the איה', which shows that this bird is famous for seeing. That fits the name ראה, 'the seer'. The ברייתא adds how far it can see.

keyTerms.meaning: Has seen it, has glimpsed it

phrases.english: And so it says:
"That path no bird of prey knows,
neither has the eye of the ayya seen it."
It was taught:
It stands in Babylonia
and sees a carcass in Eretz Yisrael.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives support to רבי אבהו's explanation of the name ראה.
steps.raayaObject: The איה is known for its sharp sight, so it fits the name ראה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: איוב 28:7 ('עין איה') and a ברייתא about it seeing from בבל to ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Then is the דאה a different bird?
steps.stepSummary: If ראה is the איה, it seems the דאה must be a separate bird. But דברים comes to add birds, so why does ויקרא write דאה while דברים leaves it out?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since ראה is איה, it follows that דאה is not ראה. But after all, משנה תורה comes to add. So why does one list write 'דאה' and the other list not write it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא works out what follows from רבי אבהו's view, then challenges that result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ראה is used up as the איה, it seems דאה must be its own bird. But the list in דברים is supposed to add to ויקרא, not leave things out. If דאה were a separate bird, דברים should not drop it.

keyTerms.meaning: It follows that, we can infer
A non-kosher bird named in ויקרא

phrases.english: Since the ra'a is the ayya,
it follows that the da'a is not the ra'a.
phrases.notes: Otherwise the count of twenty-four non-kosher birds would come up short.

phrases.english: But after all, Deuteronomy
comes to add;
what is different here, that "da'a" is written,
and what is different there, that "da'a" is not written?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּרָאָה הַיְינוּ אַיָּה, מִכְּלָל דְּדָאָה לָאו הַיְינוּ רָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests what רבי אבהו's identification means for the bird דאה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that, for רבי אבהו, דאה is a separate bird.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דברים adds birds and never leaves any out. If דאה were separate, דברים would have to list it.

steps.title: דאה, ראה and איה are one bird
steps.stepSummary: The only way out is to say that, for רבי אבהו, דאה, ראה and איה are all one bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that דאה, ראה and איה are one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the problem from the last step: all three names are the same bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If all three names mean one bird, nothing is missing from דברים. It simply uses a different name for the same bird.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this, conclude from this

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it so? Learn from this
that da'a and ra'a and ayya are one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For רבי אבהו, דאה = ראה = איה.

steps.title: Then is the דיה a different bird?
steps.stepSummary: If ראה is the איה, it seems the דיה must be separate. But then why does ויקרא put 'למינה' on the איה, while דברים puts it on the דיה?
steps.simpleTranslation: And since ראה is איה, it follows that דיה is not איה. Then why does one list write 'after its kinds' on the איה, and the other list write it not on the איה but on the דיה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא runs the same test again, this time for the bird דיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It seems the דיה should now be a separate bird. But the switch of 'למינה' from איה in ויקרא to דיה in דברים, the point used in step 4, shows they are one bird.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-kosher bird named in דברים

phrases.english: And since the ra'a is the ayya,
it follows that the dayya is not the ayya.
What is different there, that it is written
phrases.notes: Here 'there' is ויקרא and 'here' is דברים, the same point as step 4.

phrases.english: "after its kinds" on the ayya,
and what is different here, that it is not written
"after its kinds" on the ayya but on the dayya?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדְּרָאָה הַיְינוּ אַיָּה, מִכְּלַל דְּדַיָּה לָאו הַיְינוּ אַיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same kind of test from step 11 to the דיה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that, for רבי אבהו, דיה is a separate bird.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'למינה' switch between the lists shows איה and דיה are one bird.

steps.title: All four names are one bird
steps.stepSummary: For רבי אבהו, דאה, ראה, דיה and איה are all one bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that דאה, ראה, דיה and איה are one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts both conclusions together: all four bird names refer to one bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 joined דאה, ראה and איה. This step adds the דיה. So רבי אבהו ends up with four names for a single bird, which leaves only 23 non-kosher birds instead of the 24 in רב's count. That is the practical meaning of 'פליגא' in step 9.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אבהו, דאה, ראה, דיה and איה are four names for one bird. The earlier view instead made two pairs (ראה = דאה, איה = דיה).

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this

phrases.aramaic: דָּאָה וְרָאָה דַּיָּה וְאַיָּה אַחַת הִיא
phrases.english: that da'a and ra'a, dayya and ayya are one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves step 13 and combines it with step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי אבהו, all four names are one bird.

steps.title: A hundred non-kosher birds of the איה family
steps.stepSummary: איסי בן יהודה teaches that there are a hundred non-kosher birds in the East, all kinds of איה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: איסי בן יהודה says there are a hundred non-kosher birds in the East, and all of them are kinds of איה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא about how big the איה family is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says the איה comes 'with its kinds'. איסי בן יהודה shows how wide that is: a hundred different birds all count as איה.

phrases.english: It was taught: Isi ben Yehuda says:
There are one hundred non-kosher birds in the East,
and they are all kinds of ayya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from naming the birds to how many birds belong to the איה family.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hundred non-kosher birds in the East are all kinds of איה.

steps.title: Counting fish, grasshoppers and birds
steps.stepSummary: אבימי teaches that there are seven hundred kinds of fish, eight hundred kinds of grasshoppers, and birds without number.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבימי son of רבי אבהו taught: there are seven hundred kinds of fish, eight hundred kinds of grasshoppers, and birds are without number.
steps.whatsHappening: A second ברייתא gives numbers for different kinds of creatures. It also sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fish and grasshoppers get exact numbers, but birds are called countless. The next step will ask how that fits with the Torah's list of birds.

phrases.english: Avimi, son of Rabbi Abbahu, taught:
There are seven hundred kinds of fish,
and eight hundred kinds of grasshoppers,
and birds are without number.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second teaching about numbers of species.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 700 kinds of fish, 800 kinds of grasshoppers, countless birds.

steps.title: But the Torah lists only twenty-four birds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: how can birds be countless? The non-kosher birds number only twenty-four.
steps.simpleTranslation: Birds? They are twenty-four!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אבימי's statement that birds are countless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah gives a fixed list of twenty-four non-kosher birds. So non-kosher birds cannot be called countless.

phrases.english: Birds? They are twenty-four!
phrases.notes: He means the twenty-four non-kosher birds listed in the Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the last clause of step 16.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah's list of non-kosher birds has a fixed number, twenty-four.

steps.title: The countless birds are the kosher ones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the wording: kosher birds are without number.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: and kosher birds are without number.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by fixing the wording of אבימי's teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah counts only the non-kosher birds. All other birds are kosher, and those really are too many to count.
steps.whatToRemember: The Torah lists a set number of non-kosher birds. Kosher birds are without number.

phrases.english: Rather, say: "and kosher birds
are without number."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the objection of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that non-kosher birds are countless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The countless birds are the kosher ones; the non-kosher ones are counted in the Torah.

steps.title: The Torah lists the smaller group: kosher animals, non-kosher birds
steps.stepSummary: רבי teaches that because non-kosher animals outnumber kosher ones, the תורה lists the kosher animals. Because kosher birds outnumber non-kosher ones, the תורה lists the non-kosher birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is taught that רבי says: God knows that there are more non-kosher animals than kosher ones, so the verse lists the kosher animals. God knows that there are more kosher birds than non-kosher ones, so the verse lists the non-kosher birds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא explaining why the תורה lists kosher animals but lists non-kosher birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the last steps: kosher birds are countless and there are only 24 non-kosher birds. The תורה always lists the shorter group, and everything else falls into the other group. So for animals it names the kosher ones, and for birds it names the non-kosher ones.

keyTerms.meaning: The One Who spoke and the world came into being, meaning God

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the תורה lists the kosher birds. For birds it lists only the non-kosher ones, and any bird not on that list is kosher.

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi says:
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no other name means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: It is revealed and known before
the One Who spoke and the world came into being
that non-kosher animals are more numerous than the kosher ones,
therefore the verse listed the kosher ones.
It is revealed and known before
the One Who spoke and the world came into being
that kosher birds are more numerous than the non-kosher ones,
therefore the verse listed the non-kosher ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ לִפְנֵי מִי שֶׁאָמַר וְהָיָה הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the correction in Step 18 that kosher birds are countless, by explaining why the תורה lists the non-kosher birds instead.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תורה lists the smaller group: kosher animals and non-kosher birds.

steps.title: What is this teaching us?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what lesson רבי's ברייתא is meant to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the point of רבי's statement is. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing which group is bigger does not seem to change any הלכה. So the גמרא wants to know what practical lesson comes out of it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? (What is the new point?)

phrases.english: What is it teaching us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the purpose of the ברייתא in Step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson comes from knowing why the תורה lists one group and not the other.

steps.title: Teach your student the short way
steps.stepSummary: The lesson matches the teaching of רב הונא in the name of רב (some say in the name of רבי מאיר): a person should always teach his student in a concise way.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like what רב הונא said in the name of רב, and some say רב הונא said in the name of רב in the name of רבי מאיר: A person should always teach his student in a short way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא teaches a lesson about teaching: just as the תורה lists the shorter group, a teacher should explain things the short way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not adding a new הלכה. It shows the תורה being efficient, and that becomes a model for how a teacher should teach.
steps.whatToRemember: The תורה lists the smaller group to stay short. From this we learn to teach students concisely.

phrases.english: It is like what Rav Huna said in the name of Rav,
and some say: Rav Huna said
that Rav said in the name of Rabbi Meir:
A person should always teach his student
in a short way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא teaches the value of concise teaching, following the תורה's model.

steps.title: A kosher bird may be eaten based on a tradition
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק rules that a kosher bird may be eaten based on a מסורת, and a hunter is believed when he says his teacher told him this bird is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: A kosher bird may be eaten based on a tradition. The hunter is believed to say: This bird is kosher, my teacher passed this down to me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: you can know a bird is kosher from a tradition, and a hunter is trusted to report that tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of checking the bird for signs, one may rely on a tradition passed down from a teacher. The hunter's word that he received this tradition is accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: A tradition passed down that a bird is kosher
My teacher passed it down to me

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of eating only birds that have a known מסורת that they are kosher.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
A kosher bird may be eaten based on a tradition,
the hunter is believed to say:

phrases.aramaic: עוֹף זֶה טָהוֹר, מָסַר לִי רַבִּי.
phrases.english: This bird is kosher, my teacher passed this down to me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: עוֹף טָהוֹר נֶאֱכָל בְּמָסוֹרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from listing birds to a practical way of knowing a bird is kosher.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A kosher bird may be eaten based on a tradition, and a hunter is believed to report it.

steps.title: The teacher must know the birds and their names
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds a condition: this only works when the teacher is familiar with the birds and their names.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: That is only when he is expert in them and in their names.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן limits רבי יצחק's rule. The tradition counts only if the teacher really knows the birds and what they are called.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every teacher's word is enough. The one who passed down the tradition must be an expert in the birds themselves and in their names. It is not yet clear which 'teacher' is meant, and that sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: That is only when (adds a condition)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
That is only when he is expert in them and in their names.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the teacher who passed down the tradition, and 'them' means the birds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וְהוּא שֶׁבָּקִי בָּהֶן וּבִשְׁמוֹתֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to רבי יצחק's rule in Step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tradition is accepted only from a teacher who knows the birds and their names.

steps.title: Which teacher: the Torah scholar or the hunter?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks whether 'his teacher' means the hunter's Torah teacher (a חכם) or the hunter who taught him to hunt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked: Is it his teacher the חכם, or his teacher the hunter?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא asks who the 'teacher' in this rule is. This question sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hunter said 'my teacher passed it down to me.' That could mean the חכם who taught him Torah, or the older hunter who trained him. The answer decides whose expertise matters.

keyTerms.meaning: His teacher who is a Torah scholar
His teacher who is a hunter

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira asked:
Is it his teacher the Sage, or his teacher the hunter?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי זֵירָא: רַבּוֹ חָכָם, אוֹ רַבּוֹ צַיָּיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of 'my teacher' in Steps 22 and 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the teacher whose tradition counts is a Torah scholar or a hunter.

steps.title: Proof from רבי יוחנן's words: it means the hunter
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן required expertise in the birds and their names. A חכם might know the names from learning, but would he recognize the birds themselves? So the teacher must be the hunter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יוחנן said, 'only when he is expert in them and in their names.' If you say it means his teacher the hunter, that fits well. But if you say it means his teacher the חכם, he may have learned their names, but does he know the birds themselves? So doesn't this prove it means his teacher the hunter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses רבי יוחנן's exact words to prove that the 'teacher' is a hunter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן required knowing the birds 'and their names,' which means knowing the birds themselves too. A חכם learns names from books and lessons, but a hunter actually sees and handles the birds. So the expert in both must be the hunter.

keyTerms.meaning: It works fine (granted, this one fits)

phrases.english: Come and hear, since Rabbi Yochanan said:
That is only when he is expert in them and in their names.

phrases.aramaic: אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבּוֹ צַיָּיד – שַׁפִּיר,
phrases.english: Granted, if you say it is his teacher the hunter, that fits well,
but if you say it is his teacher the Sage,
granted, he has learned their names,
but does he know the birds themselves?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: רַבּוֹ צַיָּיד.
phrases.english: Rather, doesn't this prove: it is his teacher the hunter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's question in Step 24 using the wording of Step 23.
steps.raayaObject: That the teacher in the rule is the hunter.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's requirement of knowing the birds themselves and not only their names.

steps.title: Conclusion: the teacher is the hunter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: learn from this that the teacher meant is the hunter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the proof and closes the question: the teacher is the hunter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's question is settled. A bird tradition counts when it comes from a hunter who really knows the birds and their names.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: A kosher bird may be eaten based on a מסורת. The tradition must come from a hunter-teacher who knows both the birds and their names.

phrases.english: Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof of Step 25.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The 'teacher' whose bird tradition counts is a hunter who knows the birds and their names.

steps.title: We may buy eggs from non-Jews anywhere
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that eggs may be bought from גויים in any place, without worrying that they came from נבלות or טרפות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: You may buy eggs from non-Jews anywhere. You don't need to worry that they came from a dead bird or from a bird with a fatal injury.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא about buying eggs from גויים. It says this is allowed anywhere, with no concern about נבלות or טרפות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry would be that the egg came from a bird that was a נבלה or a טרפה, which would make the egg forbidden. The ברייתא says we don't worry about either, since neither is likely. It says nothing yet about whether the bird itself was a kosher species, and that gap is what the גמרא attacks next.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals or birds that died without proper שחיטה
Animals or birds with a fatal defect, which are forbidden
We are not concerned; we don't worry about it

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may buy eggs from non-Jews
in any place,
and one need not be concerned
neither about carcasses
phrases.notes: The worry would be an egg taken from a bird that died without שחיטה.

phrases.english: nor about טרפות.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לוֹקְחִין בֵּיצִים מִן הַגּוֹיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from relying on a hunter's מסורת for birds to a related question: relying on גויים for eggs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eggs may be bought from גויים anywhere, with no concern about נבלות or טרפות.

steps.title: Maybe the eggs come from a non-kosher bird
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: even if we don't worry about נבלות or טרפות, maybe the eggs are from a טמא species.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the eggs are from a non-kosher bird?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem the ברייתא didn't address: the egg might come from a non-kosher kind of bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only removed the worry of נבלות and טרפות. Eggs of a non-kosher species are forbidden no matter how the bird died. So how can we buy from a גוי without knowing which bird laid the egg?

phrases.english: But perhaps they are from a non-kosher bird?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא in step 27 for leaving out the concern of a טמא species.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's blanket permission to buy eggs from גויים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Eggs from a non-kosher species are forbidden, and nothing in the ברייתא rules this out.

steps.title: The non-Jew names a specific kosher bird
steps.stepSummary: אבוה דשמואל explains that the ברייתא means a case where the גוי says the eggs are from a particular, named kosher bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל's father said: The ברייתא is talking about when the non-Jew says the eggs are from such-and-such kosher bird.
steps.whatsHappening: אבוה דשמואל answers the challenge by narrowing the ברייתא. It applies only when the seller names a specific kosher kind of bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry about a טמא bird is solved by the seller's statement. He doesn't just say 'kosher'; he names the exact species, which is known to be טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where he says
Such-and-such bird; a specific named species

phrases.english: Shmuel's father said:
It is when he says: these are of such-and-such kosher bird.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל: בְּאוֹמֵר שֶׁל עוֹף פְּלוֹנִי טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28 by limiting the ברייתא to a case where the גוי identifies the bird.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to allow buying any eggs from a גוי, even with no information about the bird.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא applies only when the גוי names a specific kosher species.

steps.title: Why must he name the species?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if we trust the גוי, why not let him simply say 'from a kosher bird'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him just say they are from a kosher bird!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes on אבוה דשמואל's answer. Why does the seller need to name a specific bird at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the גוי's word is good enough, a general statement like 'these are from a kosher bird' should work too. Requiring a named species seems like an extra detail with no purpose.

phrases.english: But let him say: of a kosher bird?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the detail in step 29 that the species must be named.
steps.kashyaTarget: אבוה דשמואל's requirement that the גוי name a specific bird.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the גוי is believed, a general claim of 'kosher' should be enough, so naming the species seems unnecessary.

steps.title: A vague claim lets him wriggle out
steps.stepSummary: If he only said 'kosher bird', he could easily dodge being caught. Naming a species makes his claim something we can check.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he would have room to slip out of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why naming the species matters. A general claim leaves the seller a way to escape if he is lying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vague 'kosher bird' can't really be tested, so a dishonest seller could deflect any question. Once he names a particular species, we can compare his eggs with known eggs of that species. Because he could be caught, he is believable.

keyTerms.meaning: To slip away; to dodge being caught

steps.whatToRemember: We rely on the גוי's word about eggs only when he names a specific kosher bird. That turns his claim into something we can check.

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: Meaning: if he only said 'a kosher bird' without naming which one.

phrases.english: he has a way to slip out of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 30 by explaining why only a specific claim is trusted.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the reason behind the requirement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A general claim of 'kosher' should be just as good.
steps.terutzMaskana: A general claim can be dodged; a named species can be checked, so only that is trusted.

steps.title: Why not just check the eggs' signs?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we rely on the גוי at all, when eggs have kosher signs we could check. It brings a ברייתא comparing egg signs to fish signs.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him check the eggs by their signs! As a ברייתא teaches: Like the signs of eggs, so are the signs of fish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question: why depend on the seller's word, when we could examine the eggs ourselves? It backs this up with a ברייתא showing that eggs have kosher signs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If kosher eggs can be recognized by physical signs, the whole discussion of trusting the גוי seems unnecessary. The quoted ברייתא proves such egg signs exist, but its wording, 'so are the signs of fish', will itself be questioned in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Signs; physical features that show something is kosher

phrases.english: But let him check by the signs!
As it is taught: Like the signs of eggs,
so are the signs of fish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling how the גוי is trusted, the גמרא asks why we need his word at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need to rely on the גוי's statement about the eggs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Eggs have their own kosher signs (shown by the ברייתא), so we could inspect them directly.

steps.title: Fish signs are already in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to the ברייתא's wording: fish signs don't need to be learned from eggs, since the תורה states them outright.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think it means the signs of fish? The תורה says 'fins and scales'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to question the wording of the ברייתא it just quoted. A ברייתא wouldn't need to teach fish signs through eggs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The signs of a kosher fish, סנפיר וקשקשת, are written clearly in the תורה. So 'like egg signs, so are fish signs' can't mean it is teaching us the fish signs. The wording must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (this can't be right)
Fins and scales, the תורה's signs of a kosher fish
The Merciful One, meaning ה׳ in the תורה

phrases.english: Could it enter your mind that it means the signs of fish?
The Merciful One said 'fins and scales'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's phrase 'so are the signs of fish'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fish signs are stated in the תורה, so a ברייתא wouldn't need to teach them by comparing them to eggs.

steps.title: Fixing the wording of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to reread the ברייתא's wording: 'Rather, say: so are the signs of...'. The corrected phrase continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: So are the signs of...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to correct the ברייתא's wording so it makes sense. The sentence is cut off here and finishes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With אלא אימא, the גמרא admits the words 'signs of fish' can't be read literally. It is about to tell us what the ברייתא really compares egg signs to, and we'll see the rest of the sentence next.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say; a phrase used to reread or fix a source's wording

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop here thinking the answer is complete. The words 'כך סימני' are the start of a sentence that finishes in the next section.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
so are the signs of

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to step 33 by starting to correct the ברייתא's wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be teaching the signs of fish.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's wording is being corrected; the corrected version continues in the next section.
